Drivers' championship standings for a season, optionally after a given round

rows.vgi.doc_llm: One row per driver in the drivers' championship. Pass a season for the final (or latest) standings, and round := N for the standings after round N. Points are exact decimals. constructor_id is null when a driver raced for more than one team that season; constructor_ids lists every team.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Drivers' championship standings. `round := N` returns the table as it stood after round N. `position` is null for unclassified drivers while `position_text` keeps the published marker.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Final 2024 drivers' championship.", "sql": "SELECT position, driver_name, constructor_name, points, wins FROM f1.main.driver_standings(2024) ORDER BY position"}, {"description": "The 2024 championship after round 10.", "sql": "SELECT position, driver_name, points FROM f1.main.driver_standings(2024, round := 10) ORDER BY position LIMIT 5"}]

Drivers who entered a season, or every World Championship driver

rows.vgi.doc_llm: One row per driver with identifier, code, permanent number, name, date of birth, and nationality. Use it to find driver_id values for other functions. Without a season it returns all ~880 drivers since 1950 (several upstream pages).
rows.vgi.doc_md: Driver reference data. `driver_id` is the key used by every other Jolpica function.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "The 2024 grid.", "sql": "SELECT driver_id, driver_code, driver_name, nationality FROM f1.main.drivers(season := 2024) ORDER BY family_name"}]

Lap-by-lap times and running positions for one Grand Prix (1996 onwards)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: One row per driver per lap of one race, with running position and lap time. Requires season and round; pass driver_id := '...' to fetch a single driver cheaply. A full race is roughly 1,000-1,400 rows fetched over 10-15 upstream pages.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Race lap times from 1996 onwards. Filtering by `driver_id` is pushed to the API and is much cheaper than filtering in SQL.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Max Verstappen's laps in the 2024 Chinese Grand Prix.", "sql": "SELECT lap, position, lap_time FROM f1.main.lap_times(2024, 5, driver_id := 'max_verstappen') ORDER BY lap"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name":"season","type":"INTEGER","description":"Championship season year"},{"name":"round","type":"INTEGER","description":"Round number within the season (1 = first race)"},{"name":"race_name","type":"VARCHAR","description":"Grand Prix name"},{"name":"lap","type":"INTEGER","description":"Lap number"},{"name":"driver_id","type":"VARCHAR","description":"Stable Jolpica/Ergast driver identifier"},{"name":"position","type":"INTEGER","description":"Running position at the end of the lap"},{"name":"lap_time","type":"VARCHAR","description":"Lap time as published, for example 1:41.528"},{"name":"lap_time_seconds","type":"DECIMAL(10,3)","description":"Lap time in seconds as an exact decimal"}]

Pit stops for one Grand Prix (2011 onwards)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: One row per pit stop in one race: driver, stop number, lap, and pit-lane duration. Durations are entry-to-exit pit-lane times, not stationary times; red-flag stops can be many minutes long.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Pit stops from 2011 onwards. `duration_seconds` is an exact decimal.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Fastest pit-lane times in the 2024 Chinese Grand Prix.", "sql": "SELECT driver_id, lap, duration_seconds FROM f1.main.pit_stops(2024, 5) ORDER BY duration_seconds LIMIT 5"}]

rows: SELECT driver_id, lap, duration_seconds FROM f1.main.pit_stops(2024, 5) ORDER BY duration_seconds LIMIT 5
Grand Prix qualifying classifications with Q1, Q2, and Q3 times

rows.vgi.doc_llm: One row per driver per qualifying session with Q1/Q2/Q3 lap times as published and as exact seconds. Pass round := N for one event or omit it for the season. Qualifying position is not always the starting grid (penalties); use race_results().grid for that.

rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name":"session_key","type":"INTEGER","description":"OpenF1 session key"},{"name":"meeting_key","type":"INTEGER","description":"OpenF1 meeting (race weekend) key"},{"name":"driver_number","type":"INTEGER","description":"Car number of the driver in this session"},{"name":"date","type":"TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE","description":"Time of the radio message, in UTC"},{"name":"recording_url","type":"VARCHAR","description":"Link to the official audio clip on Formula 1 live timing"}]
rows.vgi.title: F1 Team Radio Clips (OpenF1)

rows: SELECT driver_number, count(*) AS clips FROM f1.main.team_radio(9472) GROUP BY driver_number ORDER BY clips DESC
